solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Recite the rosary, holding a rope

indicators.note: to hold something is to contain it, so the answer sits inside the preceding words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Someone praying with beads, clutching a rope as they go.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer spans reciTE THE Rosary; the religious picture distracts from simply reading the letters in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A tether is a cord or line used to tie an animal to a fixed post, which is exactly a rope.

clue.text: Article bobbing around a water channel

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one part wraps the other
something bobbing moves up and down unsettled, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, as the fodder
taken as written

explanation.surface: A newspaper article, or some object, bobs about near a waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' looks like it will give A or THE, but the whole word is the fodder, wrapped round the separate 'a'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailrace is the channel that carries water away from a mill wheel or turbine after use.

clue.text: Take advantage of endless ribbon

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: tape is a narrow strip of material

explanation.surface: Someone exploits a ribbon that never stops.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for the ribbon loses its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To tap a resource, as in tapping into talent, is to draw on it and exploit it.

clue.text: Old king got up on pick-up truck to make careful speech

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means rising from bottom to top, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: Old King Cole of the nursery rhyme
a ute is an Australian utility vehicle

explanation.surface: An aged monarch climbs onto a lorry to give a measured address.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the second. Old King Cole is the merry old soul of the English nursery rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: To elocute is to speak in a studied, declamatory manner with deliberate pronunciation and delivery.

clue.text: Spread stories backing daughter: record is very good

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the string that follows is read from its end

parts.note: standard abbreviation for daughter
an extended-play record
taken as written
so means very, as in 'so kind'
standard abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A gossip column item: tales about a daughter, and her record is excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing daughter' looks like supporting her, but 'backing' turns round the whole wordplay string, not just one word. 'Very good' splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To gossip is to pass on rumours and tittle-tattle, so having spread stories is the past tense verb.

clue.text: After some deliveries, article is on shelf for unrestricted purchase

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries, and 'over' also means after
the definite article
a counter is a flat surface in a shop

explanation.surface: Once the delivery van has been, a product is shelved and available to all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deliveries' suggests a shop's stock arriving, but it is cricket, where a bowler's six balls make an over. Being over also means being finished, after.
explanation.definitionFit: Medicines sold over-the-counter need no prescription, so any customer may simply buy them in a shop.

clue.text: Drunken Caledonian clubs ejected

indicators.note: something ejected is thrown out, so those letters are removed

parts.note: Caledonia is the Latin name for Scotland
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A tipsy Scot is thrown out of the golf club or nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: The drunken Scot is a comic stereotype; here 'Caledonian' supplies the longer word and the clubs are the card suit to be removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sottish describes someone like a sot, a habitual drunkard, so it means stupefied with drink.

clue.text: Proud, fervent speech praising the railway?

parts.note: pro means in favour of
the Tube is the London Underground railway
a rant is an impassioned tirade

explanation.surface: A haughty enthusiast delivers a passionate tribute to trains.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces run in the reverse order to the clue. 'Proud' looks like arrogant, but it is the sense of sticking up above a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Proud in its physical sense means projecting slightly from a surface, which is what bulging or swelling outwards describes.

clue.text: Birds no longer suffice as stuffing for cooks

indicators.note: stuffing sits inside a bird, so one part fills the other

parts.note: to do food is to cook it
that will do means that will be enough

explanation.surface: Chefs find birds are no longer enough for the stuffing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuffing' fits the kitchen scene but is purely a placement instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: These large flightless birds of Mauritius are extinct, so they are birds that exist no more.

clue.text: Around sunset, fag break?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the hour from which vehicles must show lights
second meaning: the moment for lighting a cigarette

explanation.walkthrough: A fag is British slang for a cigarette, and lighting up means igniting one. The question mark flags the playful second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The official period from dusk when road users must switch on lamps, and equally the moment a smoker ignites a cigarette.

clue.text: Ad-libbing station jingle is foolish

parts.note: improv is improvised performance, made up on the spot
an ident is the short musical or visual signature of a broadcast station

explanation.surface: A radio station's made-up jingle is judged a silly idea.
explanation.walkthrough: IDENT is broadcasting jargon for the brief clip that identifies a channel between programmes.
explanation.definitionFit: Improvident means failing to provide for the future, a lack of prudence that counts as unwise behaviour.

clue.text: Curious old method of payment

parts.note: standard abbreviation for old
DD is a direct debit, a bank instruction to pay regularly

explanation.surface: Someone remarks on a strange, antiquated way of paying.
explanation.walkthrough: A direct debit is a standing arrangement letting a company take payments from a bank account.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something strange or unusual, making them straightforward synonyms as adjectives.

clue.text: Improve painting that's thoroughly wet: what a pain

parts.note: to ret is to soak flax or hemp to soften it
the cry of someone hurt

explanation.surface: An artist complains that fixing a picture still soaking wet is a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: RET is a textile term for steeping plant stems in water until the fibres separate.
explanation.definitionFit: Retouching is making small corrections or enhancements to a picture or photograph after it is done.

clue.text: Four-footers balance unsteadily, suspicious at first around vehicle

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the earlier pieces wrap the next one

parts.note: to teeter is to wobble on the edge of balance

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word before

parts.note: the first letter of the word
a tram is a street railway car

explanation.surface: Four-legged animals wobble, wary at first of a passing car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Four-footers' suggests animals, but the feet are metrical, units of rhythm in verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetrameter is a line of poetry containing four metrical feet, so the plural are lines of that length.

clue.text: Popular champion throwing kid jokily into the air

indicators.note: throwing one thing into another places it inside, as the following 'into' confirms

parts.note: an air is a melody
to rib is to tease someone in fun

explanation.surface: A well-loved sports hero tosses a child playfully up high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' looks like a child being thrown in the air, but it is a verb meaning to tease.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Rome a tribune was an official who protected the interests of the common people against the patricians.

clue.text: Woman martyred with stiletto or revolver perhaps during annual festivities

parts.note: St Catherine of Alexandria was martyred, traditionally on a spiked wheel
standard abbreviation for with
a stiletto is a thin high heel

explanation.surface: A murder story: a woman killed with a dagger or a gun at a yearly celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: Stiletto and revolver suggest weapons; one is a shoe heel, the other anything that spins. The annual festivities are Bonfire Night, 5 November, when Britain lets off fireworks.
explanation.definitionFit: This firework is pinned to a post and spins round showering sparks, a rotating device lit at the November celebrations.

clue.text: Shown veiled

definitions.meaning: first meaning: broadcast or projected, as a film is
second meaning: hidden behind a partition

explanation.walkthrough: The two meanings pull in opposite directions, displayed and concealed, which is the whole trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A film shown in a cinema has been projected, while something hidden behind a partition has been concealed, both senses of one word.

clue.text: Drink that has naval ratings finally bouncing wildly

indicators.note: acting wildly means without order, so these letters are rearranged freely

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the closing letter of that word is kept

parts.note: the last letter of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: Sailors lurching about wildly after a drink or two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ratings' look like sailors to go with 'naval', but only the last letter is used. Ratings are ordinary sailors below officer rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauvignon blanc is a crisp white wine made from a green grape variety, so it is an alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Bad boy's two homes

parts.note: the first home: a villa is a country house
the second home: in means at home

explanation.surface: A wayward lad has a couple of houses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two homes' gives two separate pieces, a house and the word meaning at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A villain is a wicked person or a criminal, so a rogue, or in the setter's phrasing a naughty lad.

clue.text: Soil is black, say, except initially round the edge

parts.note: B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black
e.g. means for example
a rim is the circular edge of something round

indicators.note: initially means at the beginning, so only the opening letter of that word is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A gardener remarks that the earth is dark apart from a lighter border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soil' looks like a noun for earth, but it is the verb to dirty. The last two pieces go in the reverse of their clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: To begrime is to make something dirty with ingrained grime, the verb sense of making mucky.

clue.text: Capital of a country in Africa British wanted back

indicators.note: wanting something back means it returns the other way, so the string is read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written
Togo is a West African country
standard abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: Britain wanted to recover the money it had put into an African state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' suggests invested money in the surface, but it is a capital city in South America.
explanation.definitionFit: Bogota is the seat of government and largest city of Colombia, its chief city.

clue.text: Drink too much? That's a coincidence

parts.note: over means excessively, as in overdo
to lap is to drink as a cat does

explanation.surface: Someone wonders if they drank too much, then shrugs it off as a fluke.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are read in reverse order to the clue: 'too much' goes first, then the drink. 'Coincidence' here means occupying the same space or time, not chance.
explanation.definitionFit: Where two things partly occupy the same space or period, they coincide in part, which is a partial sharing.

clue.text: Close match, one's rarely worn out

parts.note: nigh means near
a tie is a sporting fixture, as in a cup tie

explanation.surface: A tight contest, and one player's shoes or kit are hardly ever used up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worn out' reads as exhausted, but here it means worn outdoors. A cup tie is British for a knockout match.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightwear such as a nightdress is kept for bed and seldom put on to go outside the house.

clue.text: Person regularly taking tablet

parts.note: to be on a drug is to take it habitually
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet

explanation.surface: Someone who routinely takes a pill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' tempts a solver to take alternate letters, but none of the words yields the answer that way; it belongs with 'taking'.
explanation.definitionFit: One is used as a pronoun for an unspecified individual, as in 'one never knows', standing in for someone.

clue.text: A bible going out for primate in Asia

indicators.note: going out suggests things breaking loose and scattering, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, part of the mix

explanation.surface: A missionary's scripture is sent off to an ape in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going' does double work in the surface but letter-wise is part of the fodder, with only 'out' left to signal the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: This long-armed ape lives in the forests of South-East Asia, such as Borneo and Sumatra, an example of a monkey-like mammal.

clue.text: Bowled over by quiet dance

parts.note: cricket scoring abbreviation for bowled
cricket scoring abbreviation for over
p is piano, the musical direction for softly

explanation.surface: Someone is overwhelmed by a gentle, slow dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowled over' reads as one phrase meaning amazed, but it splits into two cricket abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: To bop is to jig about informally to pop music, a lively bit of dancing.

clue.text: One missing a work meeting told to go inside

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: inside places one part within another

parts.note: a bee is a gathering for communal work, like a sewing bee
someone sent away has been told to go

explanation.surface: Someone skips a work meeting and is ordered to come in.
explanation.walkthrough: A bee in the American sense is a social gathering to get a job done together, such as a quilting bee.
explanation.definitionFit: An absentee is a person who is not present where expected, such as at school or work.

clue.text: Security on door vital at flat

parts.note: key means crucial, as in a key point
pad is informal for a home or flat

explanation.surface: Good door locks are essential in an apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' reads as British for apartment, and that is the sense, but the word needed is the slangy pad.
explanation.definitionFit: A numbered panel beside an entrance, into which a code is typed to unlock it, is a common access control device.
